The primary paper is unavailable and the exact percentage has weaker independent corroboration, but ISMG independently supplies sufficient support under the contract. The different 15-step statistic is not counterevidence.

semantics.note: The normalization reasonably captures the claim that the new findings reinforce earlier findings of similar vulnerabilities.

contract.note: Consistent findings at greater scale fairly operationalize the comparison. A February revision qualifies because Marcus did not claim the earlier work first appeared that month.

evidence.note: The February 2 revision documents sequential tool-chaining vulnerabilities with attack success above 90% in most cases. The September first release does not negate the February revision.
The July version identifies UC Berkeley and AWS affiliations. It provides authorship context; its revised results are not evidence of February findings.
The pre-cutoff report connects the February AWS/Berkeley findings with the new study's similar tool-chaining vulnerabilities and added production scale.

reviews.rationale: The February STAC revision documents the relevant attack class, and ISMG reports matching vulnerabilities at production scale in the new study. The September 2025 first release does not contradict a statement about findings shown in February. Identification of the unnamed paper remains inferential but is supported by the matching description and dates.
